paths.learner_scope: Career-entry learners progressing to an entry/junior Flutter role. General computer literacy is assumed; prior programming or Dart experience is not. Teach Dart natively only to the depth required to implement Flutter applications. General Git operations, systematic debugging, code review and CI/CD mechanics belong to prerequisite Software Engineer coverage, not new Flutter concepts. Reuse equivalent HTTP, JSON, testing and other foundations from this run's global concept registry snapshot through the later registry delta as prerequisite coverage; a registered concept with a planned destination is not evidence that its teaching already exists, so unmet prerequisite coverage must be flagged rather than assumed. Apply these foundations in Dart and Flutter without duplicating their generic teaching. The scope budget governs all later inventories: target 130 final atomic concepts, hard ceiling 150, about eight per benchmark capability family and never more than twelve per family; retain all required capabilities and cut least job-critical breadth when needed. The twelve benchmark families are the only capability structure. Include only skills or decisions a junior developer is expected to perform unaided in the first six months; preserve atomicity rather than bundling unrelated targets or fragmenting widget options to manipulate counts. Supplied exercise scaffolding, API contracts, native handlers and environment fixtures are materials, not prerequisite concepts, and must be declared as supplied scaffolding in the semantic dependency report. Native Android/iOS programming, server-side API implementation, game development, advanced graphics/animation engines and low-code builders are outside scope. Other cross-platform frameworks, desktop/web targets, custom native-plugin authoring, advanced performance tuning and complex CI/CD construction are also excluded as unnecessary breadth for this mobile entry/junior claim.
